It's a {d}damn tough {A}life full of {d}toil and {a}strife we {d}whalermen {a}under{d}go.
And we don't give a {A}damn when the {d}gale is {a}stopped how {B}hard the {a}wind did {d}blow.
For we're {F}homeward bound from the {C}Arctic ground with a {d}good ship, taut and {A}free.
And we {d}don't give a {A}damn we {d}drink our {A7}rum with the {d}girls of {a}old {d}Maui.

Rolling {F}down to Old Maui{C}, me boys, rolling {B}down to Old Maui{A}.
We're {d}homeward {A}bound from the {d}Arctic {a}ground, rolling {d}down to {a}Old {d}Maui.

Once more we sail with a northerly gale through the ice and wind and rain.
Them coconut fronds, them tropical lands we soon shall se again.
Six hellish months have passed away on the cold Kamchatka Sea.
But now we're bound from the Arctic ground, rolling down to Old Maui.

Once more we sail with a northerly gale towards our island home.
Our mainmast sprung, our whaling done, and we ain't got far to roam.
Our stuns'l bones is carried away, what care we for that sound?
A living gale is after us, thank God we're homeward bound.

How soft the breeze through the islands trees, now the ice is far astern.
Them native maids, them tropical glades are awaiting our return.
Even now their big brown eyes look out hoping some fine day to see 
Our baggy sails runnin' 'fore the gales, rolling down to old Maui.
title: Rolling Down To Old Maui
